affected_groups: People dependent on northern food systems
alternative_explanations: Mobility and resource disputes can have non-climatic drivers.
uncertainty: Policy-brief risk through 2080; scenario unspecified and no causal conflict estimate.
compact_statement: Northern livelihood pressures may contribute to mobility and resource tensions.

climate_pressure: Heat stress and changing availability of water and fodder.
documented_impact: Reported changes in herding/feeding practices can lead to crop damage or contested tree use.
fcv_mediator: Land/tree tenure rules, resource allocation, politicized identities and limited trust/enforcement in dispute institutions.
possible_consequence: The Gushegu account describes verbal disputes and warns of escalation; climate is an exacerbating factor, not the primary or sufficient cause.
alternative_explanations: Political mobilization, land acquisition, population pressure, crop damage, stigmatization and weak dispute mechanisms independently shape tensions.
uncertainty: A 2022 case-based brief and interviews, not a climate-attributable conflict estimate or current incident map. Ethnic identity is not treated as a propensity for violence.
resilience_factors: Inclusive, trusted dispute resolution is relevant; committee existence alone is not evidence of enforceable or fair outcomes.
compact_statement: In Gushegu, reported heat-related herding adjustments can encounter crop/tree-tenure disputes within a politically mediated conflict setting; no independent climate effect is estimated.
